subject: Q4 why no independent prompt state; CompactionEntry.systemMessage snapshot
text: There is no separate durable prompt-state field or file in coding-agent sessions: the ordered SystemMessage entries in the transcript ARE the prompt/tool state. SessionManager persists each system-role prompt message as a normal SessionMessageEntry (agent-session.ts _handleAgentEvent message_end branch includes role==='system'); replay via getCurrentSystemMessage/getCurrentTools derives the current sections, content and offered tools. AgentSession._restoreToolsFromTranscript() on startup reads every system message on the branch (including those before a compaction), calls getCurrentTools to restore the loadout, then adds extension tools that the branch never mentioned and applies +name/-name modifiers. The one extra snapshot is CompactionEntry.systemMessage: appendCompaction() calls getCurrentSystemMessage(this.buildSessionProjection().messages) and stores the complete replayed SystemMessage with timestamp=new Date(entry.timestamp).getTime(); sessionEntryToContextMessages(compaction) returns [entry.systemMessage, compactionSummaryMessage] so the prompt precedes the summary. buildContextEntries drops raw system-message entries before firstKeptEntryId, so this snapshot preserves prompt/tools across summarization. Reason: baseline + section patches + tool deltas are sufficient to reconstruct the exact current prompt and tool set, duplicating them in separate state would risk divergence. The durable harness spec (packages/durable/docs/spec.md section 7.4) states the same principle: it has no durable prompt sections; the transcript's positional system entries are the only durable record of what the model saw.

subject: Q2 buildSessionProjection and context_edit projection semantics
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts buildSessionProjection(entries,leafId,byId): gets thinkingLevel/model via getSessionContextSettings(path); contextEntries=buildContextEntries(...); builds edits = Map<targetId,ContextEditEntry> by iterating contextEntries in order and calling edits.set(entry.targetId,entry) for every entry.type==='context_edit', so the LATEST edit for a target wins. It maps each sourceEntry to ProjectedSessionEntry: if sourceEntry.type==='compaction' && index>0 then messages=[] (an older compaction kept inside the newest retained range must not contribute a second summary); otherwise messages=projectContextEntry(sourceEntry,edits.get(sourceEntry.id)). projectContextEntry: messages=sessionEntryToContextMessages(entry); no edit => unchanged; edit.replacement===null => [] (target omitted); otherwise map each message: only roles user/assistant/toolResult/custom get content replaced, returning {...message,content}; for assistant or toolResult a string replacement.content is normalized to [{type:'text',text:replacement.content}], while user/custom keep the string; role, usage, toolCallId, timestamp and other metadata are preserved. context_edit entries themselves contribute no messages. The projection returns {entries,messages:flatMap(entry.messages),thinkingLevel,model}; buildSessionContext returns the same messages/thinkingLevel/model. sessionEntryToContextMessages(compaction) returns [entry.systemMessage, createCompactionSummaryMessage(entry.summary,entry.tokensBefore,entry.timestamp)] when systemMessage exists, else just the compaction summary.

subject: Q5 estimateProjectedContextTokens usage invalidation and fallback estimate
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts estimateProjectedContextTokens(projection,branchEntries): first estimate=estimateContextTokens(projection.messages). If estimate.lastUsageIndex is null it returns that pure estimate. Otherwise it maps the projected message index that supplied the usage back to its ProjectedSessionEntry.sourceEntry.id by walking projection.entries and accumulating entry.messages.length until lastUsageIndex < nextMessageIndex; finds that id's index in branchEntries (usageEntryIndex); scans branchEntries backwards for the latest entry whose type is 'context_edit' or 'compaction' (latestInvalidatingEntryIndex). If usageEntryIndex > latestInvalidatingEntryIndex, the usage is still valid and the estimate is returned unchanged (usageTokens>0, lastUsageIndex set). Otherwise the old usage is invalidated and the function recomputes purely: tokens=estimateTokens(getCurrentSystemMessage(projection.messages)) when a system message exists, plus estimateTokens(message) for every projection message whose role!=='system'; returns {tokens,usageTokens:0,trailingTokens:tokens,lastUsageIndex:null}. Thus a usage captured at or before any later context_edit or compaction is never trusted; usage captured strictly after the newest invalidating entry is trusted. session-context-edit.test.ts verifies pre-edit usage is not trusted, post-edit usage is trusted, usage before a later compaction is not trusted, and the fallback includes the effective system prompt and tool declarations.

subject: Q1 compact() merges history summary and turn-prefix summary
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts compact(preparation,...): if preparation.isSplitTurn && preparation.turnPrefixMessages.length>0, it produces TWO summaries and merges them. historyText starts as preparation.previousSummary ?? 'No prior history.'; if preparation.messagesToSummarize.length>0 it calls generateSummaryWithUsage(messagesToSummarize, model, undefined, apiKey, headers, signal, customInstructions, previousSummary, thinkingLevel, streamFn, env, retry, callbacks, sessionId), sets historyText=result.text and historyUsage=result.usage. Then generateTurnPrefixSummary(turnPrefixMessages,...) uses TURN_PREFIX_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT and returns {text,usage}. Merged summary = historyText + two newlines + '---' + two newlines + '**Turn Context (split turn):**' + two newlines + turnPrefixResult.text. summaryUsage = historyUsage ? combineUsage(historyUsage,turnPrefixResult.usage) : turnPrefixResult.usage (combineUsage sums input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens/cost fields). If not a split turn it makes one generateSummaryWithUsage call. After the summary branch, computeFileLists(fileOps) yields {readFiles,modifiedFiles}; summary += formatFileOperations(readFiles,modifiedFiles), which appends <read-files> and <modified-files> blocks separated by blank lines. Returns {summary,firstKeptEntryId,tokensBefore,usage:summaryUsage,details:{readFiles,modifiedFiles}}. getSummarizationFailure throws on response.stopReason==='error' or 'length'; a response containing toolCall throws 'Summarization attempted to call a tool'.

subject: Q3 durable JSONL layout and commit protocol: sidecars, main.jsonl marker, fsync, commit point
text: packages/durable/src/storage/jsonl/storage.ts: FORMAT_VERSION=1; MAIN_FILE='main.jsonl'; sidecar names sidecarFileName('doc',DocumentId)='doc-<id>.jsonl' and ('task',TaskId)='task-<id>.jsonl'; temp files are '<file>.reclaim'. MainMarker = {format:1,type:'commit',seq:Seq,writes:MainOperation[]}. MainOperation variants: 'conversation'/'entry'/'submission' carry the full record inline; 'task' carries the full record inline ONLY when value.state.status==='terminal'; 'document.retire' carries id; 'task.sidecar' carries {id,ordinal}; 'document.create' carries {record:DocumentCreate,ordinal}; 'document.change' carries {id,ordinal}. SidecarRecord = {format:1,type:'record',seq,ordinal,payload:{type:'task',value:StoredTask}|{type:'document',id:DocumentId,content:DocumentContent}}. encodeCommit(seq,writes) assigns one global ordinal per sidecar record in write order (nextOrdinal++, starting 0), groups records per sidecar file, serializes each record as one JSON line, and builds one marker JSON line. Non-terminal task state and every document base/delta live only in sidecars; terminal task state, conversation/entry/submission records and document retire operations live inline in main.jsonl. packages/durable/src/storage/jsonl/storage.ts JsonlStorage.commit(writes,adopt,context): (1) prepared=this.memory.prepareCommit(writes) validates/detaches and assigns seq; (2) encoded=encodeCommit(prepared.seq,prepared.writes); (3) planReclamations(prepared.writes,encoded); (4) for every affected sidecar, appendFile its complete encoded content (all records of this commit for that file) BEFORE the marker; (5) if options.fsync (JsonlStorageOptions.fsync, default false) call flushFile on every affected sidecar; (6) appendFile the single main.jsonl marker line. The marker append is the commit point ('The marker is appended: the batch is durable'). After it: prepared.apply() updates MemoryStorage, adoptSidecarState() tracks current-only docs/live task sidecars, adopt(seq) is called exactly once synchronously, then reclaimSidecars(reclamations) runs best-effort AFTER adoption (so publication never waits for reclamation). If fsync is true, reclaimSidecars first flushes main.jsonl (making the marker durable before old sidecar data is deleted/rewritten), then replaceSidecar writes '<file>.reclaim' (flush if fsync) and renameFile over the sidecar; content '' means remove. Storage contract in types.ts: once a batch is durable call adopt(seq) exactly once synchronously before the next commit starts, then resolve; a commit failing before durability never calls adopt. Any sidecar/main append or flush failure poisons the storage (JsonlStoragePoisonedError) and later operations reject until reopen.

subject: Q5 tokensBefore computation, recomputation and compaction trigger
text: tokensBefore: prepareCompaction computes tokensBefore=estimateProjectedContextTokens(buildSessionProjection(pathEntries),pathEntries).tokens before findProjectedCutPoint; compact() carries it through unchanged; AgentSession.appendCompaction(summary,firstKeptEntryId,tokensBefore,...) stores it in CompactionEntry.tokensBefore. An extension-provided CompactionResult may supply its own tokensBefore. For compaction entries appended from session boundary drafts, _applyBoundaryDrafts recomputes at append time: estimateProjectedContextTokens(manager.buildSessionProjection(),manager.getBranch()).tokens. After append, the reported CompactionResult.estimatedTokensAfter is estimateMessagesTokens(buildSessionProjection().messages) = sum estimateTokens over messages; it is not stored in the entry. shouldCompact(contextTokens,contextWindow,settings) returns settings.enabled && contextTokens > contextWindow - settings.reserveTokens (strict >; DEFAULT_COMPACTION_SETTINGS = {enabled:true,reserveTokens:16384,keepRecentTokens:20000}). In _checkCompaction, direct contextTokens=calculateContextTokens(assistantMessage.usage) is used only when the projection has no context_edit entries, stopReason is not 'error', and usage is non-zero; any context edit forces estimateProjectedContextTokens; for error or all-zero usage it calls estimateContextTokens and skips compaction when the last usage assistant timestamp <= the newest compaction entry timestamp (stale pre-compaction usage).

subject: Q6 SQLite documents/document_revisions and JSONL document sidecar storage
text: SQLite (packages/durable/src/storage/sqlite/schema.ts, migrations.ts, storage.ts): table documents(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT, family INTEGER 0|1, key_value TEXT, scope_kind CHECK('session','conversation','task'), owner_id INTEGER, created_at INTEGER, retired_at INTEGER, record TEXT JSON). table document_revisions(document_id INTEGER, seq INTEGER, kind TEXT CHECK('base','delta'), version INTEGER, content TEXT JSON, PRIMARY KEY(document_id,seq)); index document_revisions_by_kind on (document_id,kind,seq DESC); indexes documents_by_address (kind,scope_kind,owner_id,family,key_value,created_at DESC,retired_at), documents_by_scope, documents_by_scope_kind. On document.create insert the documents row with createdAt=seq and insert a base revision. On document.change insert one revision row (base or delta); a base for a current-only document (scope!='conversation' or history='latest') first DELETE FROM document_revisions WHERE document_id=?; a delta requires a previous revision and the same version. On retire set retired_at/record and delete all revisions for current-only documents. Reads pick the newest base with seq<=at, then apply deltas with seq>base.seq and seq<=at in order, requiring identical version; deltasSinceBase=tail.length. JSONL (packages/durable/src/storage/jsonl/storage.ts): each document incarnation has 'doc-<id>.jsonl'; every SidecarRecord payload is {type:'document',id,content:DocumentContent} and main.jsonl carries document.create/document.change markers with the record/id plus ordinal. After the marker commits, current-only document sidecars are rewritten to the latest base and retired current-only sidecars are removed; rewindable sidecars are never reclaimed. Recovery truncates current-only sidecar records before the latest base and drops unconfirmed tails. Live task data uses task-<id>.jsonl sidecars; terminal task records are inline in main.jsonl and the task sidecar is removed.

subject: Q1 prepareCompaction slicing, firstKeptEntryId, messagesToSummarize, turnPrefixMessages
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts prepareCompaction(pathEntries,settings): returns undefined if pathEntries has length>0 and its last entry type is 'compaction'. It builds projection=buildSessionProjection(pathEntries); prevCompactionIndex = first projected entry with sourceEntry.type==='compaction' && messages.length>0 (the newest projected compaction); previousSummary = that CompactionEntry.summary; boundaryStart = prevCompactionIndex+1 (else 0); boundaryEnd = projectedEntries.length; tokensBefore = estimateProjectedContextTokens(projection,pathEntries).tokens; cutPoint = findProjectedCutPoint(projectedEntries,boundaryStart,boundaryEnd,settings.keepRecentTokens). firstKeptEntryId = projectedEntries[cutPoint.firstKeptEntryIndex].sourceEntry.id (undefined => return undefined). historyEnd = cutPoint.isSplitTurn ? cutPoint.turnStartIndex : cutPoint.firstKeptEntryIndex. messagesToSummarize = projectedEntries.slice(boundaryStart,historyEnd).flatMap(getMessagesFromProjectedEntryForCompaction): that helper returns [] for sourceEntry.type==='compaction' and filters out message.role==='system'. turnPrefixMessages = cutPoint.isSplitTurn ? projectedEntries.slice(cutPoint.turnStartIndex,cutPoint.firstKeptEntryIndex).flatMap(same helper) : []. If both arrays are empty => undefined. fileOps = extractFileOperations(messagesToSummarize,sourceEntries,prevCompactionIndex) plus extractFileOpsFromMessage for every turnPrefixMessages when splitting. Returns {firstKeptEntryId,messagesToSummarize,turnPrefixMessages,isSplitTurn,tokensBefore,previousSummary,fileOps,settings}. findProjectedCutPoint computes cut points from ProjectedSessionEntry.messages (context-edit-aware) and, when the budget was exceeded and the suffix is a closed recovery-omission suffix (contains an omitted assistant attempt, no external replacement, only inherently invisible/omitted entries), advances cutIndex by 1; metadata alone never moves the cut past unsent input.

subject: Q5 calculateContextTokens and estimateContextTokens algorithm
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts: calculateContextTokens(usage) returns usage.totalTokens || usage.input + usage.output + usage.cacheRead + usage.cacheWrite (native totalTokens preferred, note output is included in the fallback). getAssistantUsage(msg) accepts only role==='assistant' with usage, stopReason not 'aborted' and not 'error', and calculateContextTokens(usage)>0. getLastAssistantUsage(entries) scans SessionEntry[] backwards for type==='message' and returns the first valid usage. estimateContextTokens(messages): finds the last valid assistant usage by scanning messages backwards; if none returns {tokens:sum estimateTokens(all messages),usageTokens:0,trailingTokens:same,lastUsageIndex:null}. Otherwise usageTokens=calculateContextTokens(usage), trailingTokens=sum estimateTokens(every message after the usage index), tokens=usageTokens+trailingTokens, lastUsageIndex=that index. estimateTokens is a chars/4 ceiling heuristic: system = content text chars (non-text image blocks count ESTIMATED_IMAGE_CHARS=4800 each) + all sections string lengths + JSON.stringify(toolsAdded).length; user/custom/toolResult = content chars; assistant = text + thinking + toolCall name + JSON.stringify(arguments); bashExecution = command.length+output.length; branchSummary/compactionSummary = summary.length. So the estimate deliberately overestimates tokens.

subject: Q1 findCutPoint algorithm and oversized user-message span result
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts: findCutPoint(entries,startIndex,endIndex,keepRecentTokens) builds cutPoints with findValidCutPoints: indices of non-compaction entries whose sessionEntryToContextMessages(entry) contains a role in {user,assistant,bashExecution,custom,branchSummary,compactionSummary}; toolResult is never a cut point. It walks backwards from endIndex-1, skips zero-token entries, adds estimateTokens of every context message (tool results included), and when accumulatedTokens >= keepRecentTokens sets cutIndex = cutPoints.find(candidate => candidate >= i) ?? cutPoints[last]. It then moves cutIndex back over adjacent entries that are non-compaction and contribute zero context messages. Returns CutPointResult {firstKeptEntryIndex,turnStartIndex,isSplitTurn}: startsTurn = isTurnStartEntry(entries[cutIndex]); if startsTurn then turnStartIndex=-1 and isSplitTurn=false, otherwise turnStartIndex=findTurnStartIndex(entries,cutIndex,startIndex) and isSplitTurn = turnStartIndex !== -1. No valid cut points => {firstKeptEntryIndex:startIndex,turnStartIndex:-1,isSplitTurn:false}. CANONICAL OVERSIZED USER SPAN: when one user-message span (one user message plus its assistants/tool results until the next user message) exceeds keepRecentTokens, the backwards accumulation crosses the budget before the span's opening user message, so the cut lands at an assistant message inside the span: firstKeptEntryIndex = that assistant entry, turnStartIndex = index of the span's user message, isSplitTurn = true. Example in packages/coding-agent/docs/compaction.md 'Split user-message spans'; test/compaction.test.ts [system,user,assistant] with keepRecentTokens=1 yields firstKeptEntryIndex=assistant (firstKeptEntryId=assistant.id), isSplitTurn=true, turnPrefixMessages=[user]. EDGE: if the single user message itself is the entry where accumulated reaches the budget (everything after it is under budget), the user is itself a valid cut point, so firstKeptEntryIndex=user index, turnStartIndex=-1, isSplitTurn=false, and no split-turn prefix summary is made.

subject: Q2 ContextEditEntry null/string/latest-edit/branch-relative/raw-history semantics
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts defines ContextEditEntry = {type:'context_edit',targetId:string,replacement:{content:ContextEditableContent}|null}. appendContextEdit(targetId,replacement) validates: replacement is null or an object containing string/array content; target exists; target is on the ACTIVE branch (getBranch()); target is custom_message or a message whose role is user/assistant/toolResult. For assistant/toolResult a string replacement is stored normalized to [{type:'text',text}]. Semantics: (1) replacement:null omits the target's entire contribution from model context; (2) a string/array replacement replaces only the message content, not role/usage/toolCallId/timestamp; (3) latest edit wins because buildSessionProjection overwrites edits.set(targetId) in path order (replace -> null -> replace yields the last text); (4) branch-relative: only context_edit entries present in the current leaf path's buildContextEntries output are collected, so branching to the target before the edit restores the original projection and an edit on another branch has no effect (test/session-context-edit.test.ts 'keeps edits branch-relative'); (5) raw history is preserved: the target entry is never mutated, the edit is a separate append-only entry, and getEntry/getBranch/session file keep the original raw message. A post-compaction edit can edit a pre-compaction retained entry; an edit that lies before the newest compaction's firstKeptEntryId is dropped with the summarized prefix. Omitted raw entries remain in storage for exports/search/billing but add no model messages, cut points, summaries, or token estimates.

subject: Q4 system prompt sections: baseline SystemMessage and subsequent section patches
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts: buildSystemPromptSections(options) returns ordered SystemPromptSections. 'preamble' is untagged: customPrompt if supplied, otherwise the default pi preamble plus generated 'tools','rules','docs' sections. Every other section is stored wrapped as '<name>\n<content>\n</name>' (addendum for appendSystemPrompt, project_context for contextFiles, skills, cwd with backslashes replaced by '/', plus custom sections). Custom section names must match /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/ and may not be 'preamble'. buildSystemPromptState(input) returns {content:'',sections} normally, or {content:input.forceSystemPrompt} with no sections when forceSystemPrompt is set. In packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts, _preparePromptAndToolLoadout(options,messages) computes patch=diffSystemPromptSections(getCurrentSystemMessage(messages)?.sections ?? {}, buildSystemPromptSections(options)); it returns undefined if nothing changed, else {role:'system',content:'',sections:patch,timestamp:Date.now()}. diffSystemPromptSections emits a value for every changed section and null for every previous section missing from current. On the first prompt previous={} so this patch contains the FULL section baseline; it is prepended to the prompt messages and persisted by the message_end handler in _handleAgentEvent as a normal SessionMessageEntry (role 'system'). Later prompts/turns persist only section deltas. Agent initial state may also prepend a leading SystemMessage via createInitialSystemMessage(systemPrompt,tools) in packages/ai/src/utils/transcript.ts when systemPrompt or tools is non-empty.

subject: Q3 JSONL seq/ordinal and structural validation rules
text: packages/durable/src/storage/jsonl/storage.ts validation: parseMainMarker requires format===1, type==='commit', Number.isSafeInteger(seq) && seq>=1, and an array writes; every operation is structurally validated: conversation/entry/submission value must be an object with safe-integer id; task must have value.id, value.state object and state.status==='terminal'; document.retire must have safe-integer id; task.sidecar/document.create/document.change require safe-integer id/ordinal and ordinal>=0. parseSidecarRecord requires format 1, type 'record', seq>=1, ordinal>=0, payload object; task payload must have value.id and a non-terminal state; document payload must have safe-integer id and DocumentContent with version>=1, kind 'base' plus object value or kind 'delta' plus ops array. Seq is the strictly increasing atomic-storage-commit sequence (types.ts: gaps permitted); ordinals are per-commit sidecar record numbers starting at 0 and unique across all sidecar records of one commit. The main marker list may repeat sidecar references only if each key is different; confirming the same [file,seq,ordinal] twice throws 'Sidecar record is confirmed more than once'. A JsonlStoragePoisonedError means an I/O failure occurred; the instance must be reopened. JsonlCorruptionError means the on-disk log itself is malformed/inconsistent. StorageRequestError is reserved for invalid reads (e.g. as-of read of a current-only document).

subject: Q3 JSONL crash recovery, torn lines, unconfirmed tails, sidecar reclamation
text: packages/durable/src/storage/jsonl/storage.ts recover(context): readLines(main.jsonl) and every sidecar; if a file is non-empty and its last byte is not 0x0a, it truncates the file at lastIndexOf(0x0a)+1 (a torn final line is discarded; with no newline the file becomes empty). Complete lines are decoded with a fatal UTF-8 decoder and parsed; malformed complete lines throw JsonlCorruptionError. Every '*.reclaim' file is deleted at open. Main markers must have strictly increasing seq. Sidecar records are validated and must be strictly ordered per file by (seq,ordinal): previous.seq > current.seq or equal seq with current.ordinal > previous.ordinal, else 'Sidecar records are out of order'. Replays markers in order, confirming each referenced sidecar key JSON([file,seq,ordinal]): missing required record => 'Missing confirmed sidecar record'; duplicate confirmation => error; optional missing is allowed for terminal tasks (terminal state inline in main) and reclaimed documents (retired current-only, or record before the document's latest base). document.create with missing/reclaimed content becomes a placeholder base {kind:'base',version:1,value:{}}. Each marker's resolved writes are applied through memory.prepareCommit(writes,marker.seq).apply(); invalid state => 'Invalid committed state at sequence'. After replay, for each sidecar file any unconfirmed record must be a suffix; a confirmed record after one throws 'Confirmed record follows an unconfirmed tail'; the unconfirmed tail is truncated at its first byte offset. Retained lines are then reclaimed: terminal task sidecar => empty; retired current-only doc => empty; current-only doc with a latest base => keep only records at/after that base. Finally currentOnlyDocuments and liveTaskSidecars are restored. Thus sidecar data appended by a crash before the marker is unconfirmed and dropped.

subject: Q4 toolsAdded/toolsRemoved declaration and transcript replay to current prompt/tools
text: Tool declarations are positional SystemMessage deltas. packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts declareToolChanges(context,pendingMessages): replays offered tools with getCurrentTools([...context.messages,...baseline]); computes getToolStateChanges(previousTools, context.tools.map(toToolDeclaration)). toolsAdded contains complete Tool definitions (toToolDeclaration = name, description, JSON-roundtripped parameters, optional constrainedSampling); toolsRemoved contains ToolReference objects {name}; a changed definition appears in both. If a pending system message exists, its toolsAdded/toolsRemoved fields are replaced with this delta; otherwise a new {role:'system',content:'',timestamp} message is inserted before the first non-system pending message. Every message_start/message_end system message is persisted. Replay in packages/ai/src/utils/transcript.ts: getCurrentTools iterates system messages in order, deletes every toolsRemoved name then sets every toolsAdded tool by name in a Map, returning [...values()] (a re-declared name replaces in place; a removed-then-readded name moves to the end). getCurrentSystemMessage iterates all system messages, appends each non-empty content with two newlines, applies sections patches in order (string sets, null deletes), computes tools via getCurrentTools(), and takes the first system message's timestamp. getCurrentSystemPrompt renders content plus all non-null section values joined by two newlines via getSystemMessageText. collapseSystemMessages returns the replayed head plus all non-system messages; resolveTranscript uses it when supportsMidConvoSystemMessages is false.

subject: Q6 DocumentRecord history latest/rewindable and fork semantics
text: packages/durable/src/types.ts DocumentRecord = {id:DocumentId,kind:string,key?:string,createdAt:Seq,retiredAt?:Seq} plus scope {kind:'session'} | {kind:'conversation',conversationId} | {kind:'task',taskId}. Only conversation documents declare history/fork: history:'latest' allows fork:'current'|'initial'; history:'rewindable' allows fork:'asOf'|'current'|'initial' (fork 'asOf' requires rewindable). An incarnation's lifetime is half-open createdAt <= at < retiredAt; ids are never reused and retiring+recreating creates a new incarnation. history:'latest' retains only current state; storage rejects as-of reads with StorageRequestError 'does not retain historical content'. history:'rewindable' retains history addressable by snapshotAsOf; a base bounds replay but never permits removal of addressable history. Fork behavior (packages/durable/src/session/forks.ts prepareForkDocumentCopies): for a fork at visible entry E, documents of the parent conversation visible at E's commit with fork:'asOf' are copied as of that commit; documents current in the parent with fork:'current' are copied from the committed parent value when the fork commit runs; fork:'initial' copies no instance (the child creates it from definition initial() on first access). Each copied instance gets a new DocumentId in the child conversation, preserves kind/key/history/fork, and starts with an initial base materialized from the source's stored value/version (document.copy, resolved backend-side). Task documents and Session documents are never copied. A transaction that creates a fork while changing a parent fork:'current' document is rejected so the source revision is unambiguous.

subject: Q2 buildContextEntries latest compaction + firstKeptEntryId projection
text: packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts buildContextEntries(entries,leafId,byId): buildSessionPath walks root->leaf (leafId or the last entry). It scans the path and keeps the LAST entry of type 'compaction' as `compaction` (newest compaction). If none, returns the full path. compactionIdx = path.findIndex(entry.id===compaction.id). Result contextEntries starts with [compaction]. It loops path[0..compactionIdx): foundFirstKept is set true when entry.id===compaction.firstKeptEntryId; from then on it pushes each entry EXCEPT a message entry whose message.role==='system'. Finally it pushes path.slice(compactionIdx+1). Thus older summarized entries are omitted, the newest compaction summary is first, entries from firstKeptEntryId up to the compaction are retained, and all entries after the compaction are retained. If firstKeptEntryId is not found on the path, no pre-compaction entries are kept. If firstKeptEntryId===compaction.id (retain-none, as appendCompaction(null) does), the result is [compaction,...entries after it]. System-role message entries before the compaction are skipped because CompactionEntry.systemMessage carries the prompt snapshot; system patches after the compaction remain in the kept tail. Function is exported and mirrored by SessionManager.buildContextEntries() using getEntries()/leafId/byId.

subject: Q6 DocumentContent base/delta and checkpointWhen conversion
text: packages/durable/src/types.ts DocumentContent = {version:number,kind:'base',value:JsonObject} | {version:number,kind:'delta',ops:readonly Op[]}. document.create always stores a complete base (definition initial value, or migrated value). For an ordinary document.change the Session prepares a Chord operation delta; at settlement, after every validation, packages/durable/src/session/transaction.ts (settleSuccess -> #assemble) evaluates definition.checkpointWhen(prepared.value, prepared.ops, {deltasSinceBase}) exactly once. deltasSinceBase = the number of deltas already stored after the incarnation's newest base, excluding the change being evaluated. If checkpointWhen returns true, the planned content is replaced by {version,kind:'base',value:prepared.value}; otherwise the prepared delta {version,kind:'delta',ops} is stored. Creation and version transitions/migrations require a base and do not call checkpointWhen. A committed base permits physical reclamation of older records for session/task/latest-conversation documents; for rewindable conversation documents bases only bound replay and never delete addressable history. Every definition must supply checkpointWhen (no default; ()=>false means only required bases, which can leave an unbounded delta tail). The predicate only selects storage representation; it does not change scope/lifetime/history/fork semantics.
